Class definition of the native YAEL image pipeline

Source: R/class011-YAEL_native_process.R
YAELNativeProcess.Rd

Rigid registration across multiple types of images, non-linear normalization from the native brain to common templates, and mapping of template atlases or regions of interest back to the native brain, without 'Python'. The class has the same methods, arguments and active fields as YAELProcess and writes the same files (names, folders, 'ANTs'-compatible .mat and warp files, 'JSON' logs), so the results of one class can be read by the other. The registrations, bias-field correction and tissue segmentation come from ravetools (version 0.3.3 or later). See examples at as_yael_process (with engine = "native") and yael_preprocess_native.

Details

Differences from YAELProcess and the rpyANTs pipeline behind it:

  • There is no deep_atropos: argument use_antspynet of map_to_template is ignored, and the tissue segmentation with the template priors (the Atropos branch) always runs.

  • The non-linear stage uses the local cross-correlation for every image (ravetools has no non-linear mutual information), also when an initial affine transform is given.

  • Algorithms: ravetools runs a greedy SyN with a single field and a fixed-point inverse; its linear stages use an automatic step size, random (Bernoulli) sampling and no histogram matching, and its affine registration starts with a rigid pass. The smoothing of the SyN update field takes the rpyANTs values (3 for the initial registration, 3.5 for the final one) as a Gaussian standard deviation in voxels, whereas ANTs reads them as a variance, so the native update field is smoothed more. These values hold for 1 mm templates; for templates with more voxels per brain they are multiplied by the cube root of the ratio of brain voxels, rounded to a half (2 for the 0.5 mm 'mni_icbm152_nlin_asym_09b' and 'mni_icbm152_nlin_sym_09b', 1.5 for the 0.25 mm macaque template): with the 1 mm values, the greedy update folded the deformation in about 1.5 percent of the brain on 'mni_icbm152_nlin_asym_09b'. The share of the template brain mask where the final deformation folds (is not one-to-one) is logged, with a warning above 1 percent.

  • The quick three-class segmentation that finds the white matter for the intensity normalization runs on the raw image, as in rpyANTs; when a few extreme intensities inside the brain leave one of its classes empty (Atropos keeps going, ravetools stops), it is run again with the intensities clipped at their 99.9 percent quantile inside the brain (then at the 99 percent quantile).

  • White-matter artifacts: the template brain mask can take in a thick, bright skull marrow, which the tissue segmentation labels as white matter and the final registration would pull into the brain. Each white-matter voxel casts one ray away from the center of the white matter; when the ray misses the smoothed outer surface of the gray matter and the cerebellum (ravetools::mris_outer_surface), the voxel is taken to lie outside the brain. These voxels, dilated by two voxels, are left out of the white-matter channel, and those labeled white matter also leave the brain mask and the brain image of the final registration; the cone below the center of the white matter, which holds the brain stem, is kept, and the removed volume is logged. The tissue classes keep the order of their priors; when the median intensities of the CSF, gray-matter and white-matter classes do not increase, a warning is given and nothing is left out.

  • Grids: additional images are resampled onto the grid of the native 'T1w' image, and left out (with a warning) when they cover less than 95 percent of the brain mask; template tissue priors are resampled onto the grid of the template 'T1' image; the outermost voxel layer of the stored warp fields has no displacement.

  • The template brain mask is made binary (this matters for 'fsaverage', whose mask holds intensities); a tissue class whose prior is empty inside the brain is left out of the segmentation (with a warning) instead of failing.

  • Outputs: transform_image_from_template and transform_image_to_template return ieegio_volume objects; only nearest-neighbor and linear (trilinear) interpolation are available, and interpolator = "auto" follows its documented rule (YAELProcess uses nearest-neighbor); the queries never create folders; set_input_image reads the new image before it removes the old one; the 'NIfTI' data types are chosen by ieegio; normalization results are replaced together, after the new ones are complete, and stale ants<K> transforms of earlier layouts are removed; nothing is written into the template folders.

  • Streamlines: ieegio reads and writes VTK files through 'Python', so generate_streamlines_from_template skips VTK inputs (with a warning) and refuses format = "vtk"; it also refuses format = "tt" and saves TT inputs as TCK files, since ieegio cannot write TT files.

Arguments

subject

'RAVE' subject or subject ID; for native standard, this can be character code without project names, but for 'BIDS' subjects, this must be a full subject ID with project information

image_types

vector of image types, such as 'T1w', 'CT', 'fGATIR'. All images except 'CT' will be considered 'preop' (before electrode implantation). Please use 'postop' to indicate if an image is taken after the implantation (for example, 'postopT1w')

imaging_path

imaging path (path to 'rave-imaging' if not default); internally used to set the work path during serialization. Please do not set it manually unless you know what you are doing

YAELNativeProcess$map_to_template()

Normalize native brain to 'MNI152' template

Usage

YAELNativeProcess$map_to_template(
  template_name = rpyants_builtin_templates(),
  use_images = c("T1w", "T2w", "T1wContrast", "fGATIR", "preopCT"),
  native_type = "T1w",
  use_antspynet = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

template_name

which template to use, choices are 'mni_icbm152_nlin_asym_09a', 'mni_icbm152_nlin_asym_09b', 'mni_icbm152_nlin_asym_09c', and 'fsaverage'.

use_images

a vector of image types to use for normalization; default types are 'T1w', 'T2w', 'T1wContrast', 'fGATIR', and 'preopCT'. To use all available images for normalization, use wildcard "all". Images that are not registered to 'T1w' yet are registered first (a failure is reported as a warning and the image is left out)

native_type

which type of image should be used to map to template; default is 'T1w'

use_antspynet

ignored: the native engine has no deep_atropos, and the tissue segmentation always uses the template priors

verbose

whether to print out the process; default is true

...

additional tuning parameters: affine_transform (optional initial affine transform, an 'ANTs' .mat file from the template to the native image as point map; the initial registration then only runs its non-linear stage), with_skull (whether to register the images with skull; default is false), and cost_function (only 'CC', the local cross-correlation, is available; other values give a warning); other arguments are ignored

Returns

See method get_template_mapping

Usage

)

Arguments

template_name

which template is used

native_type

which native image is mapped to template

relative

whether the paths should be relative or absolute; default is false (absolute paths)

Returns

A list of input, output images, with forward and inverse transform files (usually two 'Affine' with one displacement field), or NULL if the image is not normalized to the template yet. The transforms of the subject are used; transforms whose subject entity is spelled in another letter case are used if there is only one such spelling, and the transforms of another subject only if they are the only ones and the native image was imported under that subject (with a warning)

YAELNativeProcess$generate_atlas_from_template()

Generate atlas maps from template and morph to native brain

Usage

YAELNativeProcess$generate_atlas_from_template(
  template_name = rpyants_builtin_templates(),
  atlas_folder = NULL,
  surfaces = NA,
  verbose = TRUE,
  lambda = 0.2,
  degree = 2,
  threshold_lb = 0.5,
  threshold_ub = NA,
  smooth_method = c("implicit", "explicit"),
  max_vertices = 5e+05
)

Arguments

template_name

which template to use

atlas_folder

path to the atlas folder (that contains the atlas files); every 'NIfTI' file in the folder and its sub-folders is mapped to 'atlases/<sub-folder>/<file name>' under the working directory (file names starting with a dot are skipped). Probability maps (values between 0 and 1, some fractional) are interpolated linearly, other images with the nearest neighbor

surfaces

whether to generate surfaces (triangle mesh); default is NA (generate if not existed). Other choices are TRUE for always generating and overwriting surface files, or FALSE to disable this function. The generated surfaces will stay in native 'T1' space.

verbose

whether the print out the progress

lambda, degree, threshold_lb, threshold_ub

passed to volume_to_surf

smooth_method

how to smooth the surfaces: "implicit" (default, vcg_smooth_implicit with lambda and degree) or "explicit" (mris_smooth); passed to volume_to_surf

max_vertices

surfaces with more vertices are reduced to about this many after smoothing; passed to volume_to_surf; default is 500000

Returns

Paths to the atlas (volume) files under the 'atlases' folder of the working directory

YAELNativeProcess$generate_streamlines_from_template()

Transform streamline tract files from template space to native brain space

Usage

YAELNativeProcess$generate_streamlines_from_template(
  template_name = rpyants_builtin_templates(),
  streamlines_folder = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  format = c("auto", "tck", "trk", "tt", "vtk"),
  native_type = "T1w"
)

Arguments

template_name

which template to use; the template must have been used in map_to_template prior to calling this method

streamlines_folder

path to folder containing streamline tract files ('.tck', '.trk', '.tt', or '.vtk'); all matching files are processed recursively, except VTK files ('.vtk', '.vtp'), which ieegio can only read through 'Python': they are skipped with a warning

verbose

whether to print progress; default is TRUE

format

output format for the saved streamlines; "auto" (default) preserves the original file extension, except that TT files are saved as TCK (ieegio has no TT writer); "tck" and "trk" convert every file. "tt" (no writer) and "vtk" (written through 'Python') are errors

native_type

which native image type defines the target space; default is "T1w"

Returns

Invisibly returns a character vector of the relative paths to the input streamline files that were processed (VTK files are left out); transformed files are written under fs/streamline/ from the working directory. The points of all files are transformed together; points with missing coordinates are dropped. 'Python' is never started: the files are read and written with the 'Python' support of ieegio disabled.

YAELNativeProcess$write_talairach_xfm()

Write the linear transform 'ants/mri/transforms/talairach.xfm' from native 'T1w' scanner 'RAS' coordinates to 'MNI305' space, using the affine part of the normalization created by map_to_template. For templates that are not in 'MNI152' space, the transform maps to the template space instead ('fsaverage' is already in 'MNI305' space). This method is called by construct_ants_folder_from_template.

Usage

YAELNativeProcess$write_talairach_xfm(
  template_name = rpyants_builtin_templates()
)

Arguments

template_name

template that has been used in map_to_template

Returns

The path to the transform file, invisibly

YAELNativeProcess$construct_ants_folder_from_template()

Create a reconstruction folder (as an alternative option) that is generated from template brain to facilitate the three-dimensional viewer. Please make sure method map_to_template is called before using this method (or the program will fail). The folder holds the conformed 'mri/T1.mgz', the template brain mask mapped to the native image ('mri/brainmask.nii.gz', binary), the bias-corrected image ('mri/nu.nii.gz'), its skull-stripped version scaled to 0 to 255 ('mri/brain.finalsurfs.nii.gz'), and the linear transform 'mri/transforms/talairach.xfm' written by write_talairach_xfm; if that fails, the file is removed and a warning is logged.

Usage

YAELNativeProcess$construct_ants_folder_from_template(
  template_name = rpyants_builtin_templates(),
  add_surfaces = TRUE
)

Arguments

template_name

template to use for mapping; NULL only writes 'mri/T1.mgz'

add_surfaces

whether to create surfaces that is morphed from template to local; default is TRUE. The surfaces are only created for templates with 'fs/surf' pial surfaces. Please enable this option only if the cortical surfaces are not critical (for example, you are studying the deep brain structures). Always use 'FreeSurfer' if cortical information is used.

YAELNativeProcess$get_brain()

Get three-dimensional brain model

Usage

YAELNativeProcess$get_brain(
  electrodes = TRUE,
  coord_sys = c("scannerRAS", "tkrRAS", "MNI152", "MNI305"),
  ...
)

Arguments

electrodes

whether to add electrodes to the viewers; can be logical, data frame, or a character (path to electrode table). When the value is TRUE, the electrode file under project_name will be loaded; when electrodes is a data.frame, or path to a 'csv' file, then please specify coord_sys on what is the coordinate system used for columns "x", "y", and "z".

coord_sys

coordinate system if electrodes is a data frame with columns "x", "y", and "z", available choices are 'scannerRAS' (defined by 'T1' weighted native 'MRI' image), 'tkrRAS' ('FreeSurfer' defined native 'TK-registered'), 'MNI152' (template MNI coordinate system averaged over 152 subjects; this is the common MNI coordinate space we often refer to), and 'MNI305' (template MNI coordinate system averaged over 305 subjects; this coordinate system used by templates such as 'fsaverage')

...

passed to threeBrain
